Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a couple follow-ups so we can get you a headcount-level pricing estimate for Redwood hosted API:

1) High-level ask: Productionize LLM-based summarization + answer retrieval for your client-facing dashboard.
2) Desired SLAs: 99.9% uptime, sub-300ms p50 for short summaries, regional US deployment.
3) Items we need from you for pricing: expected monthly token volume (approx range is fine), peak TPS (requests/sec) during busiest windows, and any target $/1M-token goal or budget band.

Can you share a best-effort monthly tokens estimate and peak TPS? If easier, send per-feature estimates (summaries vs. retrieval) — even rough numbers enable a helpful pricing band (hosted). I attached the simple estimate template (fincap_monthly_estimates.xlsx) — fill the three columns and send back.

Next steps: once we have the numbers I'll run a unit-economics calc showing baseline hosted cost and a dedicated-reserved estimate for comparison.

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the template. Attaching a quick-fill version. High-level estimates (rough):

- Primary feature: "Executive summaries" (short, ~120 tokens output, ~400 token context avg incl. retrieval). Estimated 1-2M requests/month -> ~480M to 960M tokens/month (aggregate; tokens incl. input+output).
- Secondary feature: "On-demand retrieval QA" (longer context, ~800 tokens avg per request). Estimated 200-300k requests/month -> ~160M to 240M tokens/month.

Combined monthly token range: ~640M to ~1.2B tokens.

Peak TPS: during product launches we see spikes ~30-40 req/sec for summaries. Typical peak TPS for the combined workload approx 45 req/sec; single-request token sizes vary so peak token-per-second could be 18k-28k tokens/sec depending on mix.

Target cost: we're aiming for ~ $20-25 / 1M tokens at scale for hosted API to fit our unit economics. Budget band for hosted in year 1: $8k- $25k/mo depending on adoption trajectory.

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood provide an expected $/1M tokens breakdown for our estimated range (both baseline hosted and with recommended batching/quantization)?
- How does Redwood handle sudden spikes (burst vs. throttling) on hosted plans?

Thanks — attaching filled estimates and SOC summary as requested.

Alex

Alex — this is great, thanks for the detail and the filled sheet. A few quick clarifying notes so we can model unit economics accurately:

1) Token math: when you say 1-2M requests/month for summaries, just confirming that estimate is the total end-user requests (not per-account). Good to know avg input+output tokens. We typically model hosted pricing using total tokens (input + output).

2) Target $/1M tokens: you noted $20-25. For your range (~640M to 1.2B tokens/mo) I can run two hosted scenarios: 
   - Baseline hosted (no quantization, standard throughput) - raw per-1M token list price + volume discount curve.
   - Optimized hosted (recommended batching, KV caching, and quantization where applicable) - expected effective $/1M token after unit savings.

3) Peak TPS: 45 req/sec combined is useful. For pricing/capacity we need to translate to peak tokens/sec. Can you confirm your conservative peak tokens/sec estimate? You mentioned 18k-28k tokens/sec depending on mix; if you can pick a planning number (e.g., 25k tokens/sec) we can size burst capacity.

What I'll send next (by EOD tomorrow): a short sheet showing (a) hosted list price bands for your token ranges, (b) recommended operational levers (batching window, cache hit assumptions) and (c) a ballpark Dedicated reserved cost for comparison (monthly commit). If you're open, I'd like to schedule a quick 30-min follow-up with Sean and our solution engineering team to walk through the unit-econ calc and SLA details - does Thu 26 Mar 10am PT work?

Best,
Marissa
